questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Formula One British Grand Prix?
questions.background: The British Grand Prix is held at Silverstone as part of the Formula One World Championship.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The race classification published by Formula One or the FIA, corroborated by contemporaneous race reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the driver classified as the winner of the British Grand Prix scheduled for July 5, 2026. Sprint results do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning driver's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 3 Silverstone reversal (FIA, Formula1.com, BBC Sport, Reuters): contrary to pre-weekend expectations that Silverstone's energy demands would bury Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton swept sole practice (1:29.260, -0.213s over Antonelli) and all three Sprint Qualifying segments to claim Sprint pole (1:28.376), edging Kimi Antonelli (1:28.387) by just 0.011s, with Max Verstappen P3 (+0.321s), Charles Leclerc P4 (+0.327s), George Russell P5 (+0.357s), Lando Norris P6 (+0.364s, minor SQ1 damage), and Oscar Piastri P7 (+0.396s). Russell admitted 'Ferrari have had the upper hand all day' and lamented his 'strange' 0.35-0.4s deficit to Antonelli, while Zak Brown confirmed McLaren still lacks the upgraded Mercedes PU. Because Mercedes (7/8 wins, 8/8 GP poles) still leads on straight-line power/deployment and teams can revise setups after Saturday's Sprint before GP Qualifying, Antonelli (0.35) retains a razor-thin edge over home 9-time winner Hamilton (0.09 -> 0.33). Russell drops sharply (0.30 -> 0.14), Verstappen trims (0.11 -> 0.08), and Leclerc (0.05, driving the quick Ferrari) replaces Norris in the top five, leaving 5% for Norris (~0.025), Piastri (~0.02), and the field.

local_articles.title: Kimi Antonelli follows up sprint victory with pole for British Grand Prix
local_articles.snippet: Kimi Antonelli took pole position for the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, seeing off a concerted challenge from Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in second and third, and his Mercedes team-mate George Russell who was fourth. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri could manage only sixth and eighth for McLaren, with four-time champion Max Verstappen in seventh for Red Bull. Antonelli held his nerve in what was a tense qualifying session, slotting in a final lap of real commitment and inch-perfect execution as he was pushed to the limit by the two Ferraris. The Italian 19-year-old, who leads the world championship and won the sprint race on Saturday morning, had almost two-tenths on Leclerc and three-tenths on Hamilton, no small margins. local_articles.title: F1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli follows up sprint win with British GP pole
local_articles.snippet: SILVERSTONE, England - Formula One leader Kimi Antonelli was too fast for Ferrari, and dealt another stinging blow to Mercedes teammate George Russell, as the Italian seized pole position for the British Grand Prix on July 4 after winning an earlier sprint race. His closest title rival Russell qualified only fourth at a windy Silverstone, behind Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and seven-times world champion Lewis Hamilton. local_articles.title: F1 leader Antonelli powers past Hamilton for first sprint win
local_articles.snippet: SILVERSTONE, England, July 4 - Kimi Antonelli blasted past home favourite Lewis Hamilton to take a first career sprint win at the British Grand Prix on Saturday and forge 43 points clear of Mercedes teammate George Russell in the Formula One standings. Ferrari's Hamilton started on pole but the seven times world champion had to settle for second place, 2.7 seconds behind, after Antonelli used the Overtake Mode to speed past on Hangar Straight -- a move he made look as easy as lapping a backmarker -- on the eighth of 17 laps. In free air, Antonelli pulled away and raced to the finish untroubled, with nothing Hamilton could do about it in the time remaining. "In control all the way," said Antonelli's race engineer Peter 'Bono' Bonnington over the team radio at the chequered flag as Antonelli became also the youngest ever sprint winner at 19 years old. questions.current_reasoning: Positive July 3 fitness update on Australia's main pre-final concern (cricket.com.au, AFP/France24, Canberra Times): Ellyse Perry completed several sprinting drills and a lengthy batting session in the nets at Lord's on Friday unscathed after Thursday's 'wellness day', with Phoebe Litchfield confirming she is 'moving really well' and on track for Sunday's final (even as she sat out fielding drills pending Saturday's final test). questions.title: Which team will win the England–India T20 international series in July 2026?
questions.background: India and England are scheduled to contest a T20 international series in England.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match results or contemporaneous AFP reporting identifying the winner of the England–India T20 international series in July 2026. Resolution Timing : Resolve when a team secures an unassailable series lead, or when the series concludes if its winner has not previously been determined. Accepted Answer Format : The country name of the series-winning team.
questions.current_reasoning: Two concrete June 30 squad updates on the eve of the July 1 series opener at Durham nudge this five-match series 3% back toward India (England 0.58 -> 0.55, India 0.42 -> 0.45): (1) ECB named England's playing XI for the 1st T20I (Salt, Buttler, Brook, Bethell, Banton, Curran, Jacks, Dawson, Rashid, Luke Wood, Saqib Mahmood—9 of their March 2026 T20 World Cup semifinal XI) with frontline fast bowlers Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue rested following the New Zealand Test series before rejoining for Match 2 at Old Trafford on July 4; (2) Sky Sports and IANS report mystery spinner Varun Chakravarthy—previously thought absent on June 28 and historically lethal against England's aggressive batting—has returned to India's 16-man squad for the England leg (though PTI's 15-man list omitted him). Durham's seam-friendly surface (138 avg T20I score), India's continuing absence of Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, and Suryakumar Yadav, and lingering batting vulnerability after their shock 0-2 sweep in Ireland still keep home England slight favorites (~51% Match 1 without Archer/Tongue, ~53.5% Matches 2-5 -> ~55.6% across five matches).
